name: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
note: Strikes at 228 on pressure balls where an average batter facing the same bowling would manage 156, the widest gap in the data. Nearly all of it comes in the powerplay, 224 against 156 expected across 242 balls, and he does it to pace and spin alike (229 and 222). He has been dismissed 11 times where 14.2 were expected. The sample is 275 balls over 28 matches, yet he holds first place in all 12 re-rankings.

name: Tim David
note: The finisher of the list: 206 against 159 expected in the death overs, across 163 balls. His 4.1 wins added under pressure is the most of any batter, and includes the four off Tim Southee with 4 needed off 1. Pace suits him far more than spin (198 against 139). He is as good for Australia as in the IPL, 175 and 191.

name: Abhishek Sharma
note: Sustains a strike rate of 199 over 732 pressure balls, so this is no small-sample story. He does his damage in the powerplay, 203 against 148 expected, and is quicker against spin (220) than pace (190). He gets out a little more than expected, 43 dismissals against 38.3, which is the price of the approach. For India in T20Is he strikes at 216.

name: Suryakumar Yadav
note: The most complete pressure record here: 748 balls at 180 against 149 expected, with 29 dismissals where 47.1 were expected. He scores faster as the innings goes on: 152 in the powerplay, 184 in the middle overs and 211 at the death. His lift over calmer balls is 21 runs per 100, with a range of -2 to 44 that almost clears zero.

name: Heinrich Klaasen
note: Takes spin apart under pressure: 192 against 125 expected. In the death overs he goes at 221 from 61 balls. Most of the evidence is from the IPL, 202 of his 262 pressure balls, where he strikes at 184 against 143 expected. His six off Harshit Rana with 13 needed off 6 is his biggest single ball.

name: Phil Salt
note: A powerplay specialist: 418 of his 526 pressure balls come in the first six overs, at 177 against 146 expected. He is quicker in the IPL (193) than for England (160), and better against pace (184) than spin (151). Dismissed 21 times where 29.0 were expected, so the speed has not cost him his wicket. He keeps a top-10 place in all 12 re-rankings.

name: Ashutosh Sharma
note: The second-smallest sample in the top 10 at 171 pressure balls, which is why his chance of truly belonging is 56%. What there is is striking: 210 at the death against 161 expected, and a six off Shahbaz Ahmed with 5 needed off 4. His strike rate jumps from 147 in calmer balls to 185 under pressure. 165 of the 171 balls are from the IPL.

name: Shreyas Iyer
note: His pressure strike rate of 153 is close to the 146 expected. The case for him is the death overs, 242 against 180 from 55 balls, and staying in: 18 dismissals where 26.0 were expected. He has added 2.1 wins under pressure. The record is an IPL one, 164 against 147; in T20Is he is below expectation at 121 against 143. A close call, with a 51% chance of the top 10.

name: Rajat Patidar
note: Destroys spin under pressure, 200 against 142 expected, but is below expectation against pace, 128 against 139. His place rests on his overall record more than his pressure balls: he strikes at 173 in calmer balls and 151 under pressure, and has added only 0.4 wins. That is why he keeps a top-10 place in just 5 of 11 re-rankings. All 195 pressure balls are from the IPL.

name: Harry Brook
note: An international record: 148 of his 165 pressure balls are in T20Is, at 168 against 136 expected. He is strong against pace (190 against 146) and in the powerplay (178), and ordinary against spin (133 against 125). His six off Andre Russell with 3 needed off 2 is the standout ball. On 165 balls his rank could fall anywhere from 4 to 48.

name: Jasprit Bumrah
note: Concedes 8.1 an over on pressure balls where an average bowler would go for 9.39, and does it at every stage: 7.8 in the powerplay, 8.2 in the middle overs and 8.9 at the death. Wickets are not the story, 16 against 23.0 expected; batters see him off. His estimated runs saved, 15.7 per 100 balls, is the highest of any bowler. He is also first when only IPL matches are counted.

name: Josh Hazlewood
note: The wicket-taker: 38 wickets on pressure balls where 24.4 were expected, 13 of them at the death. Economy is 8.43 against 9.39 expected. Right-handers struggle most, 7.6 against 9.1 with 28 wickets. For Australia in T20Is he goes at 6.3 an over against 8.3 expected. His 2.3 wins added is the second most in the bowling top 10.

name: Varun Chakravarthy
note: Gets better as the innings gets tighter: 6.7 an over at the death against 9.2 expected, with 6 wickets from 81 balls. He has 36 pressure wickets where 29.5 were expected. He is equally hard for right- and left-handers, 8.2 to both. For India in T20Is he goes at 7.1 against 8.2 expected. He keeps a top-10 place in all 12 re-rankings.

name: Sunil Narine
note: Concedes 6.84 an over on pressure balls where 8.69 was expected, a gap of nearly two runs an over. He does it in the middle overs, 6.8 from 282 balls, and at the death, 6.0. Right-handers get nothing: 6.3 against 8.7 expected. All 393 pressure balls are from the IPL, and he keeps a top-10 place in all 11 re-rankings that apply to him.

name: Nathan Ellis
note: A smaller sample, 249 pressure balls over 18 matches, but a clear one: 8.31 against 10.09 expected. He is best in the powerplay and middle overs, 7.7 and 7.5; at the death he is close to par at 10.2 against 10.8. He is much better to left-handers (7.2) than right-handers (9.1). 16 wickets where 13.8 were expected.

name: Bhuvneshwar Kumar
note: The largest pressure sample of any bowler in the top 10: 746 balls over 70 matches. A powerplay bowler, 504 balls at 7.7 against 8.7 expected with 30 wickets. At the death he is on par, 11.0 against 11.2. Overall he goes at 8.66 against 9.4 expected. His biggest ball is the LBW of Rovman Powell with 2 needed off 1.

name: Rashid Khan
note: Has added 2.4 wins under pressure, the most of any bowler in the top 10. He controls the middle overs at 6.9 against 8.3 expected across 455 balls, and takes wickets at the death, 19 from 124 balls. 42 wickets where 36.5 were expected. He is effective in the IPL (7.9 against 9.2) and in T20Is (6.4 against 7.6), and keeps a top-10 place in all 12 re-rankings.

name: Matheesha Pathirana
note: A death-overs bowler judged against a brutal baseline: his pressure economy of 9.05 looks ordinary until it is set against the 11.04 an average bowler would concede on the same balls. In the middle overs he goes at 7.9 against 10.2 expected. The cost is control, 14.3 wides and no-balls per 100 pressure balls, and wickets are only at par, 17 against 16.3. His record is mostly an IPL one, 175 of 228 balls. With a 33% chance of truly belonging, he is one of the closer calls.

name: Wanindu Hasaranga
note: The wicket-taker among the spinners: 33 wickets on pressure balls where 26.1 were expected. That is the case for him, because his economy of 8.63 is slightly worse than the 8.45 expected. He is better for Sri Lanka, 7.7 an over against 8.3 expected, than in the IPL, 9.4 against 8.6, and better to right-handers (8.0) than left-handers (9.4). His biggest ball is bowling Mitchell Hay with 51 needed off 30. He has the lowest chance of the ten, 30%, and holds his place in 3 of 12 re-rankings.

name: Jacob Duffy
note: One of the closer calls, with a 33% chance of truly belonging, though he keeps his place in 8 of 11 re-rankings. His case is the powerplay: 179 balls at 8.6 against 9.0 expected, with 11 wickets. He has 18 pressure wickets where 14.2 were expected. Economy of 8.92 against 9.11 expected is only slightly better than par, and his 30 IPL pressure balls went at 12.2.
